```{r setup}
#| output: false
#| code-summary: "readRDS() — load prepared objects, running 01_prepare_data.R if needed"
library(dplyr); library(here); library(knitr)

if (!file.exists(here("data", "derived", "usable.rds")))
  source(here("R", "01_prepare_data.R"))

usable <- readRDS(here("data", "derived", "usable.rds"))
funnel <- readr::read_csv(here("outputs", "funnel.csv"))
by_mon <- readr::read_csv(here("outputs", "effort_by_month.csv"))

# Monthly totals with the empty months present, so they can be named in prose.
mon <- tibble::tibble(month = 1:12) |>
  left_join(count(usable, month), by = "month") |>
  mutate(n = tidyr::replace_na(n, 0),
         name = month.name[month])

peak     <- slice_max(mon, n, n = 1)
empty    <- filter(mon, n == 0)$name
n_usable <- nrow(usable)
n_spp    <- n_distinct(usable$CommonName)
```

This is a companion note to an animated map of cetacean sighting records in the
Hawaiian Islands Exclusive Economic Zone, built from NOAA's public
[WinCruz sighting archive](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/inport/item/18141).
It sets out where the data came from, what was excluded and why, what the
seasonal pattern is, and — the part that matters most — what the map cannot be
read as saying.

## The map

```{r figure}
#| code-summary: "The seasonal animation (rendered by R/02_seasonal_map.R)"
#| fig-cap: "September, the densest month. The full twelve-month animation is at `outputs/hawaii_cetacean_seasonal.mp4`."
include_graphics(here("outputs", "figures", "still_september.png"))
```

Twelve frames, January to December, pooling all years. Each amber point is one
sighting. Bathymetry is underneath, the EEZ boundary is outlined, and the
species recorded that month are named down the right-hand side.

Plotting code is in `R/02_seasonal_map.R` rather than inline, since it runs to a
couple of hundred lines and renders 240 frames.

## What a WinCruz sighting record is

Each row is one group of one species, seen once, from a ship. The archive
carries the date, the ship's position at the start of the sighting, species,
group-size estimates, the EEZ and PIFSC region, what cued the observation,
whether the sighting was mixed-species, and the NMFS permit it was collected
under.

One absence shapes everything below: **there is no effort or trackline
information**. The archive contains sightings and nothing else. It cannot say
where the ship went, how far it steamed, or how long observers were searching.

That single fact is why this note is careful about the word "distribution".

## Filtering

Three exclusions, in order.

**Non-cetaceans.** `SpeciesCode` is numeric for cetaceans and alphabetic for sea
turtles (`CC`, `CM`, `DC`, `EI`) and Hawaiian monk seal (`MS`). One record in
the archive is not a cetacean.

**Records not identified to species.** `Unid. Dolphin`, `Unid. Beaked whale`,
`Mesoplodon sp.`, `Sei/Bryde's whale` and similar are records of *a cetacean*,
not of a species. A map that names species can only draw records that name one.

**Effort type.** From the InPort entity metadata:

> Did the sighting occur when the survey effort was systematic (S),
> non-systematic (N), fine-scale (F), or off (O)

Only `S` denotes systematic line-transect effort, where the ship is running a
planned track with observers on watch. The rest happen while transiting,
closing on a group, or otherwise not surveying — real sightings, but not
comparable between months or places. Note that `O` means **off**-effort; it
reads like "on", and filtering on it silently selects the wrong records.

```{r funnel}
#| code-summary: "The exclusion sequence, in counts"
kable(funnel, col.names = c("Step", "Records"), format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

`r format(n_usable, big.mark = ",")` sightings across `r n_spp` species remain.
Group size was deliberately *not* required: the map draws one point per
sighting regardless of how many animals were in the group, so a missing
group-size estimate is no reason to drop a record here.

## Seasonal coverage

```{r month-table}
#| code-summary: "Sightings by month and effort type, Hawaiian Islands EEZ"
#| tbl-cap: "Effort types: systematic (S) is planned line-transect effort with observers on watch; non-systematic (N) and fine-scale (F) are other on-water modes; off-effort (O) is transiting or closing on a group. Only S is comparable between months."
by_mon |>
  right_join(tibble::tibble(month = 1:12), by = "month") |>
  arrange(month) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !month, ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0)),
         Month = month.name[month]) |>
  select(Month,
         `Systematic (S)`     = S,
         `Non-systematic (N)` = N,
         `Fine-scale (F)`     = F,
         `Off-effort (O)`     = O) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The record is heavily skewed toward the second half of the year.
**`r peak$name`** alone holds `r peak$n` of the `r format(n_usable, big.mark = ",")`
systematic sightings.

`r knitr::combine_words(empty)` contain none at all.

The distinction between effort types earns its keep here. March and April are
empty of *systematic* records, but both carry sightings under other effort
types — vessels were present, they were simply not running line-transect
effort. December is the only month with no records of any kind.

So the accurate statement is not that three months went unsurveyed. It is that
systematic effort is concentrated in the second half of the year, and that the
winter record rests almost entirely on a single February.

## Cruises

```{r cruises}
#| code-summary: "Sightings by cruise — the unit the seasonal pattern actually reflects"
usable |>
  count(CruiseID, name = "Sightings") |>
  arrange(CruiseID) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Cruise", "Sightings"))
```

Nine cruises, five years. The monthly pattern above is better read as a record
of when these cruises sailed than as a seasonal schedule: 2010 and 2017 — both
HICEAS years — contribute 145 and 101 sightings respectively, two-thirds of the
total, and every cruise working in September belongs to one of them. September's
apparent peak is the HICEAS field season sampled twice.

Two of the nine are transits rather than surveys, contributing six sightings in
total. One of those six is the entire January record.

## Building the map

Two things about this region caused more trouble than the data did.

**The EEZ crosses the antimeridian.** Its bounding box in conventional
−180/180 longitude spans the entire globe, and eight sightings sit east of the
line. Everything is handled in 0–360 instead. The source polygon is also split
at 180°, and that seam survives the shift as an interior line which `geom_path`
will happily draw straight across the map; it is stripped before plotting.

**The bathymetry arrives on two different grids.** `marmap`'s antimeridian mode
fetches the halves either side of 180° separately, and they come back with
different cell sizes — 0.06694° and 0.06793°, plus a 0.035° sliver at the join.
`geom_raster` assumes a regular grid and draws every cell at one nominal width,
so the mismatch renders as vertical striping across the whole panel. The data is
resampled onto a single regular 0.07° grid, with an assertion afterwards so a
future regression fails loudly rather than quietly.

## What this map does not show

**It shows records, not animals.** With no effort data in the archive, the
points describe where observations were written down. Reading spatial pattern
from them means reading wherever the ship happened to go.

**Blank months mean no systematic effort**, not an absence of animals — and in
two of the three cases, not even an absence of survey activity.

**Species identification varies in resolution.** Around 30% of the archive is
cetaceans not identified to species, and those records are unlikely to be
distributed evenly across taxa. Excluding them is necessary for a
species-labelled map and is not neutral.

**Sightings are not corrected for detectability.** Sea state, group size and
species behaviour all affect whether an animal present is an animal seen, and
none of that is accounted for in a plot of raw records.

**Nine cruises, not twelve years.** The record spans 2009–2017 but comprises
nine cruises in five years, two of them transits. Any monthly or annual
comparison is a comparison between a handful of voyages, and a month's total can
rest on a single one — January's does.

## Data and attribution

**Sightings** — NOAA Pacific Islands Fisheries Science Center, Cetacean Research
Program. *Shipboard Cetacean Surveys — Visual Surveys — WinCruz Sighting
Records*, [InPort 18141](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/inport/item/18141).
Collected under NMFS permits `r paste(sort(unique(usable$Permit)), collapse = ", ")`.
Citing the permit numbers is a condition of use.

**Bathymetry** — NOAA ETOPO, via [marmap](https://cran.r-project.org/package=marmap).

**EEZ boundary** — Flanders Marine Institute, *Maritime Boundaries Geodatabase*
v12 (2023), [marineregions.org](https://www.marineregions.org/), CC BY 4.0.

**Silhouettes** — [PhyloPic](https://www.phylopic.org/) via
[rphylopic](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rphylopic); per-image
contributors and licences in `outputs/phylopic_credits.csv`. Three species have
no PhyloPic image and use a genus- or family-level stand-in.
